questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
I found the academic programmes that Lund University (LU) have incredibly interesting, and have thought so for a while. So for me, being able to take a course at the human ecology department, for instance, was a big motivation, and I'm happy that I did. I had also heard good things about the academic level at LU in general, so I think it was mainly an academic challenge that I was looking for. 
But I was also hoping to get a new taste of what university could also look like, having spent my bachelor's and most of my master's at the same university. So the opportunity to try out a new way of "doing" university was also thrilling.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Would recommend!

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I think it was quite easy. The only thing that I maybe would say is that the whole "nations" thing at LU was hard to figure out, and I found that I was lacking information on what it even meant to choose a nation (which felt like a big deal, especially when talking to other students and finding out that there is a long history and many connotations to the different nations).

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Hmm, I feel like the information was quite clear, but my coordinator, was good at answering my emails :)

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Hmm, I'm not sure I can answer that, since my situation was a bit special and I was commuting to Lund. But I heard that the Småland's nation was a nice place to live, so maybe check that out.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: A bit the same as above. I was commuting/taking the train to Lund, but that was also fine. The train station isn't that far from campus (obviously depends on which department - the geography one was maybe the furthest away of the ones I went to, and that took maybe 15-20 minutes to walk).

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Since I wasn't living in Lund, I don't feel that I can say anything much about how the housing availability was in Lund. So I put the middle option.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I felt it was a little difficult to understand which courses were available to exchange students, and which weren't. The selection was a bit small (even though I got some good courses). I wasn't allowed into one that I had signed up for, and then I was offered another - which was fine, but it was located in Helsingborg. So be aware that there are also some courses there (about 30 minutes from Lund by train).

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Phew, it's far away now. But you sign up in the platform called Solemove, where you can add courses in the "proposed study plan". Here, you also upload different kinds of documentation such as passport, statement of purpose etc. and information about your home university. LU very explicitly state that you have to choose many options, as you are not certain to get into your first priority courses. This is quite nice, as I probably wouldn't have if they didn't state that. But it was also a bit difficult to find enough courses and make the puzzle fit with the right amount of ECTS at the right times. The semester is divided so that you have only one course at a time (at least I did), which makes it important to be aware that you don't have too much overlap - especially because the courses were quite intense, since they were so short.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: As I wrote before, my international coordinator at LU was very helpful. It all worked out in the end, also with the courses that I couldn't join - in Solemove they then put a notice saying that I couldn't get in because of this and that, but that I could get a spot on this other course if I wanted to. So it was nice that LU proposed an alternative.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: As I have mentioned a couple of times, there was one class (7.5 ECTS) that I didn't get into. But the alternative was also fine. The other 22.5 ECTS were the ones that I wanted, which was exciting!

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Hmm, maybe to take a look at the course catalogue well in advance, and be aware that you have to choose more than just the courses that are your first priority. I think I had both second and third, because you cannot register for new courses once the registration closes (or at least that's how I understood it). 
I was at three different departments, and I thought that worked out quite well. It gave me something new at each department, so I would advise also to maybe try out different stuff - also courses that maybe lie a bit away from your core subject.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Absolutely excellent!

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
I found a pretty advanced level, and I definitely had to work to keep up. But it meant that I learned a lot!
HEKN14 was great and had high level.
GNVN33 was also good and had high level.
SMMV27 was the one that I didn't pick as a first choice, and while the level and academic expectations were probably a bit lower here, I left having learned a lot.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There was a bit more group work, seminars, presentations and hand-ins at LU, which took some getting used to. But in the end I appreciated the more interactive environment where there was an expectation to us to deliver which was probably a bit higher than at UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
HEKN14 Human Ecology: Political Ecology, Crisis and Identity (15 ECTS)
GNVN33 Gender studies: Feminist Methodologies and Methods (7.5 ECTS)
SMMV27 Assessment of Environmental Impact (7.5 ECTS)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would especially recommend HEKN14 Human Ecology: Political Ecology, Crisis and Identity which was just an amazing course. Lots of new perspectives, and a really engaged group of students and professors.
I would also recommend GNVN33 Gender studies: Feminist Methodologies and Methods.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I mostly remember the Lundakarneval which unfortunately only is every four years I think. But that was fun! Otherwise I think there were hiking trips and I know the People's Kitchen was also very popular. I never went though.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I heard good things about the people's kitchen, I would recommend that. And Lundakarnevalen if you're lucky enough to get the chance. But then I would just recommend going on all the study excursions too, at HEKN14 we had a really nice three day trip to end the course to Söderåsen, which was lovely and a very beautiful place. I would recommend going.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Maybe go to Söderåsen for a hike!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I live in Copenhagen, so it was quite easy and not that different.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Hmm, not that relevant for me, but I do think the group work made me have to be very open. But that was also good.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Honestly, I think that the Swedish alcohol culture is probably more healthy than the Danish. And that people were very serious about their studies - but still up for laughing about it. I also quickly felt very welcome.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Take courses in different departments!
There's a lot of information coming from Student Lund - I don't think you have to take in all of it.
The new courses start the day after the exams (at least they did for me). So start working on your exams as soon as possible (boring advice, I know, but it felt pretty tight, and was tough to hand in a paper Sunday evening and start a new course Monday morning).

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
The fact that there is a short time between a course ending and a new one starting. Be aware, and start reading early on. 
Also: There are many different platforms: Ladok, Solemove etc. The most important one, I think, to familiarize yourself with is Canvas (built like Absalon at UCPH).

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Definitely trying a new style of university classes! The way that people engaged with the readings was amazing.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Probably the big workload, even though it was also rewarding.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
